overview: A strong Pacific system brings rain and wind to the Cascades through Thursday, then a weak ridge gives a short break this weekend before the pattern turns active again. Snow favors the Rockies and Canadian ranges through Friday and Saturday, with the Northeast mostly rain.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A strong front brings rain and gusty wind to the Cascades through Thursday, with snow levels around 5,000 to 6,000 feet. Snow returns Friday as a weaker system moves through, and the forecasters expect a brief break this weekend under a weak ridge. Crystal Mountain leads the region with 14" in the next five days. The NWS is calling for more, 19 to 36 inches Thanksgiving Day through Monday night.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A Pacific system brings light to moderate snow west of the Divide Friday, with a stronger wave and strong westerly wind Friday night into Saturday. Jackson Hole leads the region with 14" in the next five days. The NWS is calling for more, 15 to 28 inches Thursday night through Monday night.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Rain dominates the Northeast Friday through Monday, with a special weather statement for Friday into Saturday. Mont-Sainte-Anne leads with 8" in the next five days, and Blue Mountain adds 5" early in the week.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Showers and rain dominate the Coast Mountains through Friday, with some flurries returning Sunday and Monday. Whistler leads with 15" in the next five days, mostly in the form of rain before the weekend.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Rain Thursday turns to a mix of sun and cloud Friday and Saturday, with flurries returning Sunday. Revelstoke leads with 7" in the next five days, and snow levels drop to around 1,000 metres late Thursday night.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Mild and dry through Thanksgiving, then snow arrives late Friday and runs through Saturday, mainly over the Park Range. Steamboat leads with 6" in the next five days. The NWS is calling for more, 7 to 15 inches Friday through Monday night.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 25, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Dec 6–12. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
